input.command:
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
Handle Ctrl+D gracefully in yes/no prompt

The custom yes/no prompt ignored Ctrl+D (byte 0x04), causing the
prompt to loop forever. Additionally, if read_key() returned an
UnexpectedEof error the cursor was never restored because
show_cursor was only called on the success path.

Extract the key-reading loop into prompt_yes_no_loop so the caller
always restores the cursor via show_cursor().ok() regardless of
outcome. Map Key::Char(CTRL_D) to the default selection and handle
UnexpectedEof by returning the default index.
EOF
)"

input.command:
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
Handle Ctrl+D gracefully in yes/no prompt

The custom yes/no prompt ignored Ctrl+D (byte 0x04), causing the
prompt to loop forever. Additionally, if read_key() returned an
UnexpectedEof error the cursor was never restored because
show_cursor was only called on the success path.

Extract the key-reading loop into prompt_yes_no_loop so the caller
always restores the cursor via show_cursor().ok() regardless of
outcome. Map Key::Char(CTRL_D) to the default selection and handle
UnexpectedEof by returning the default index.
EOF
)"

git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
Handle Ctrl+D gracefully in yes/no prompt

The custom yes/no prompt ignored Ctrl+D (byte 0x04), causing the
prompt to loop forever. Additionally, if read_key() returned an
UnexpectedEof error the cursor was never restored because
show_cursor was only called on the success path.

Extract the key-reading loop into prompt_yes_no_loop so the caller
always restores the cursor via show_cursor().ok() regardless of
outcome. Map Key::Char(CTRL_D) to the default selection and handle
UnexpectedEof by returning the default index.
EOF
)"
